check: correct the round-budget conclusion from the previous round
whatIReportedLastRound: A gap of about 10 rounds (1.1 hours) between what the remaining work needs and what the remaining rounds provide.
whereTheEarlierFigureWentWrong: It compared hours to rounds in a way that double-counted the post-profile work. The wall clock after the profile ends is not consumed round by round: a background job runs while rounds pass, so 5.95 hours of post-profile work costs about 10 rounds rather than 55. The earlier note applied the 55-round figure and then also charged the profile's own hours against the same budget.
theCorrectedModel: Rounds needed = profile hours remaining divided by minutes per round, plus a fixed cost of about 10 rounds for the post-profile steps. Against 167 available, 118 needed leaves 49 rounds of slack.
theOperationalGuidanceStillStands: Start the post-profile steps as background jobs in the round the profile ends, and keep each round to one substantive action. That guidance was right even though the arithmetic behind it was not - it is what makes the post-profile cost about 10 rounds instead of 55.
methodNote: The wall clock advanced 6.7 hours between rounds this time, which is why the profile now shows 12.4 hours rather than 5.7. Re-measuring against the new position is what exposed the earlier arithmetic, and it is also why a budget checked once early in a long run should be checked again near the end.
